@graph.articleBody: Most owners pick an agency the way they pick a restaurant in an unfamiliar city: a good-looking pitch, a friendly call, a quick decision. The pitch tells you very little about what happens after you sign. This checklist gives you criteria you can test before you hire anyone. One disclosure first: Etuos is a marketing agency, so we have an interest in this topic. Apply every point below to us as well. If an agency cannot pass these checks, it should not pass them for you either. Key Takeaways - D

itemListElement.name: How to Choose a Marketing Agency: A Checklist for Local Business Owners

mainEntity.name: How do I choose a marketing agency for a local business?

acceptedAnswer.text: Decide what result you need, then check each agency on the same points: what work it will do, who owns your accounts, whether it promises rankings, how it separates fees from ad spend, what its reports show, and how you can leave. Verify its claims independently.

mainEntity.name: What questions should I ask a marketing agency before I sign?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask who owns your Google Business Profile, Google Ads account and Search Console property, what exactly they will do, which numbers you will see, what they will not promise, and what happens to your accounts and data if you leave.

mainEntity.name: Can a marketing agency guarantee a first-page ranking on Google?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. For local results, Google says there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. For Search in general, it says it does not guarantee that it will crawl, index or serve your page.

mainEntity.name: Should I own my Google Ads account and Business Profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You should be the owner, with the agency added as a user. Google ties editing and customer interaction on a Business Profile to verification, and says a verified owner in Search Console has the highest degree of permissions.

mainEntity.name: How can I check whether an agency is legitimate?

acceptedAnswer.text: Search for the agency and its clients, look the advertiser up in Google's Ads Transparency Center, call references it names, and read how it handles its own reviews. Treat what you find as a starting point for questions.
